The failing test `testValidate_WritableFile` creates a `File` object representing a readable text file and sets it to be read-only. Then, it creates a list of file paths containing a writable text file path and the previously mentioned readable text file path. After that, it obtains a `FileValidator` instance using the `getExistingFileInstance` method, which sets the validator to check for an existing file that must be writable. Finally, it calls the `validate` method of the `FileValidator` with the list of file paths. The test expects an `InvalidArgumentException` to be thrown with a specific error message related to the readable file path.

The current bug report mentions an issue related to command line parsing when supplying arguments with default values. It seems to be unrelated to the failure in the test.

Looking at the code of the `getExistingFileInstance` method in the `FileValidator` class, it sets the validator to check for an existing file but does not specifically enforce writability. This discrepancy might be the root cause of the failure in the test where it expects the validator to enforce writability.

Next, I will inspect the `FileValidator` class to understand how the writability check is handled.

- `org.apache.commons.cli2.validation.FileValidator.getExistingFileInstance()`
